Prisoner 46764- Andrew Mlangeni

By: Siniketiwe Hlanze | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
The last of the Rivonia Treason Trialists has died

Unique Selling Point:
Not much is known about the senior ANC member who dedicated his life to the struggle, spending 26 years on Robben Island. As a tribute to his life and uncovering some of his contribution to the struggle and liberation movement. Interviews with some of his comrades, hid biographer and political analyst to understand the life of Andrew Mlangeni, prisoner 467/64.

Summary:
An obituary that look at Andrew Mlangeni's life alongside the country's history and trajectory of the ANC.

Script:



A loyal comrade, servant leader and revolutionary.

Andrew Mlangeni’s contribution to South Africa’s liberation struggle does not enjoy the prominence of his peers but is evident in history.

Following the African National Congress’ decision to take up arms and establish a military wing, it was Nelson Mandela who enlisted Mlangeni as the first uMkhonto weSizwe operative
Whilst his fitness test was doing push-ups with his comrade, it was his training in communist China that elevated his skills in radio technology, bomb making and military intelligence.


It was his missions as an MK trainer and recruiter working underground that would land him in trouble with the apartheid government.

The 1963 Rivonia Trial which sought to prosecute senior ANC leaders, including Mlangeni, Ahmed Kathrada, Dennis Goldberg and Nelson Mandela for their involvement in drafting the Operation Mayibuye document – an assignment that would see the possible roll out of guerrilla warfare.

To stem the resistance movement, the regime retaliated with a conviction and harsh sentence, to life imprisonment on Robben Island.

It was through this covert sharing of ideas and strategies that the friendships amongst comrades were both tested and made stronger

MAC Link At Home.

Mlangeni preferred the simple surroundings of his community and had an easy affinity with his comrades at grassroots level.


Mac Luthuli House Link


A loyal member in good standing within the party. Mlangeni witnessed his organisation become embroiled in corruption scandals, factional squabbles and its moral authority eroded.


Considered a fair arbitrator, in 2012 he was deployed to chair the party’s integrity committee - an attempt for the organisation to self correct.


Most recently he gave his support and voice to the veterans of the movement in their call for reform as attempts to self correct proved futile.
The last of his generation’s freedom fighters, a cadre who was satisfied if his only reward was getting the job done.
